description: T3a document-ranking benchmark over ZOMAH's own .md/.txt/.rst documentation. Each case names the one document that holds the evidence; evidence_anchor is a verbatim (whitespace-normalized) quote from it and is checked before scoring. Several exact/paraphrase cases share the same evidence so wording is the only variable between them.

categories.exact: Query reuses the source document's own distinctive terms.
categories.paraphrase: Asks for one specific stated fact, with the source's distinctive terms replaced by everyday wording.
categories.conceptual: Asks about a purpose, reason, or kind of thing using synonyms or broader concepts the passage never uses.
categories.distractor: Query vocabulary is shared by several documents on nearby topics; only the expected document holds the specific evidence.

cases.query: What are the six conceptual primitives that ZOMAH v0 begins with?
cases.evidence_anchor: ZOMAH v0 begins with six conceptual primitives:
cases.rationale: Only PROJECT.md lists the core domain objects (Task, Context, Worker, RunState, Trace, Verification).

cases.query: Does schema versioning use PRAGMA user_version, or is a separate migration framework required?
cases.evidence_anchor: A separate migration framework is not required for v0.
cases.rationale: Only the persistence contract names PRAGMA user_version; ADR-002 mentions migrations only as a cost.

cases.query: Do validation details echo rejected input values back to the model?
cases.evidence_anchor: Validation details identify fields and error types but do not echo rejected input values.
cases.rationale: Only ADR-005 states the no-echo rule for validation details.

cases.query: When a call is refused because its arguments were malformed, does the reply repeat what the caller originally sent?
cases.evidence_anchor: Validation details identify fields and error types but do not echo rejected input values.
cases.rationale: Same evidence as ex-validation-echo, reworded.

cases.query: What is the per-image limit for clipboard images attached with Alt+V, and how many images can a draft hold?
cases.evidence_anchor: a 10 MiB per-image limit; a draft holds at most 4 images
cases.rationale: Clipboard image limits are documented only in README.md.

cases.query: How many pictures can I stick onto one message before sending it, and how big can each one be?
cases.evidence_anchor: a 10 MiB per-image limit; a draft holds at most 4 images
cases.rationale: Same evidence as ex-clipboard-limits, reworded.

cases.query: Is each approved candidate file fingerprinted using modification time and size so unchanged documents are not re-indexed?
cases.evidence_anchor: Each approved candidate file is fingerprinted using modification time and size; unchanged documents are not re-read or re-indexed.
cases.rationale: README and ARCHITECTURE say the refresh is incremental; only ADR-007 says how unchanged files are detected.

cases.query: How does search know a note hasn't been edited since last time, so it can skip reading it again?
cases.evidence_anchor: Each approved candidate file is fingerprinted using modification time and size; unchanged documents are not re-read or re-indexed.
cases.rationale: Same evidence as ex-fingerprint, reworded.

cases.query: May the working directory of a registered automation stay writable, or is only the approved executable protected?
cases.evidence_anchor: The protected object is the approved executable itself.
cases.rationale: README and ARCHITECTURE describe digest checks; only ADR-004 addresses the writable working directory.

cases.query: If an approved script works inside some folder, is that folder locked down too, or just the program file?
cases.evidence_anchor: The protected object is the approved executable itself.
cases.rationale: Same evidence as ex-protected-executable, reworded.

cases.query: Is tool_result_budget_chars a deterministic character bound or a token estimate?
cases.evidence_anchor: This is a deterministic local character bound, not a token estimate
cases.rationale: The per-turn tool-result budget is documented only in README.md (T2d).

cases.query: Is the cap on how much tool output one reply can pile up measured in model tokens or in something simpler?
cases.evidence_anchor: This is a deterministic local character bound, not a token estimate
cases.rationale: Same evidence as ex-character-bound, reworded.

cases.query: If my terminal can't tell a modified Return key apart from a plain one, how do I start a new line while typing a message?
cases.evidence_anchor: Ctrl+J is the compatibility fallback
cases.rationale: ARCHITECTURE lists Shift+Enter as required composer behavior; only README gives the fallback for terminals without the kitty keyboard protocol.

cases.query: Can the generated project status page be saved straight into my personal note-taking app?
cases.evidence_anchor: The user may later configure an Obsidian/Vault destination without changing the persistence contract.
cases.rationale: README gives the current exports/ location of the mirror and ADR-002 mentions future knowledge-vault integration in passing; only the persistence contract says a notes-vault destination can be configured.

cases.query: When a project is finished and no longer needed, does it get wiped from the database?
cases.evidence_anchor: Projects transition to `archived` rather than being deleted.
cases.rationale: ARCHITECTURE lists 'archived' as a status value; only the persistence contract's deletion policy says projects are archived instead of deleted.

cases.query: Why wasn't the whole system built on top of an existing third-party agent runtime?
cases.evidence_anchor: ZOMAH's durable state and control boundary should not depend on OpenClaw's continued presence.
cases.rationale: PROJECT and ARCHITECTURE mention OpenClaw only as something to integrate with; only ADR-001 records rejecting it as the core runtime and why.

cases.query: Can the assistant find out which projects exist without being told an identifier first?
cases.evidence_anchor: `get_project_state` requires a known project ID.
cases.rationale: Only the capability audit discusses project discovery (a deferred watch item).

cases.query: Will the assistant look after my inbox or put appointments in my schedule?
cases.evidence_anchor: - email integration - calendar integration
cases.rationale: Only PROJECT.md's explicit non-goals rule out email and calendar integration.

cases.query: Why does keeping the set of tools tiny make it easier to debug when something goes wrong?
cases.evidence_anchor: Failures are easier to attribute to the model, context, tool, or harness.
cases.rationale: Only ADR-001's consequences connect a narrow tool surface to attributing failures.

cases.query: Why not just keep the project record in a structured config-style file on disk instead of a database?
cases.evidence_anchor: They would be simple initially but require ZOMAH to build its own locking, transactional update behavior, indexing, and relationship handling as the system grows.
cases.rationale: Only ADR-002's alternatives weigh JSON/YAML files against SQLite; the persistence contract states the rule without the comparison.

cases.query: What kinds of live machine information is the assistant meant to look at in a structured way rather than through a general shell?
cases.evidence_anchor: This is intentionally preferred over unrestricted shell inspection.
cases.rationale: README only says 'explicit Linux system domains', and the audit and ADR-006 mention process/service/mount entries only as output budgets; ARCHITECTURE lists the inspect_system domains as the alternative to shell inspection.

cases.query: When there are too many past choices to show the assistant, which ones get shown first?
cases.evidence_anchor: currently active lifecycle states (`proposed` and `accepted`) are prioritized before terminal historical states
cases.rationale: ARCHITECTURE and README mention a bounded decision window; only ADR-006 says which decisions are prioritized.

cases.query: What is the current stdout limit for run_script results returned to the model?
cases.evidence_anchor: stdout: 16 KiB
cases.rationale: The capability audit quotes the older 64 KiB stdout limit it asked to reduce; ADR-006 holds the adopted budget.

cases.query: How many passing tests did the capability audit record as its baseline?
cases.evidence_anchor: 83 passing tests
cases.rationale: PROJECT.md reports a later baseline (121 passing tests); only the audit records its own.

cases.query: Why not store every state change as an event log and rebuild the current state from it?
cases.evidence_anchor: ZOMAH needs current truth plus useful provenance, not a complete event-sourced architecture.
cases.rationale: The persistence contract lists event sourcing as a non-goal and ARCHITECTURE/PROJECT say history belongs elsewhere; only ADR-002 gives the reason for rejecting it.

cases.query: Did the capability review conclude that embeddings were needed for knowledge retrieval?
cases.evidence_anchor: SQLite FTS5 lexical retrieval is working well and is sufficient for v0. Embeddings are not justified.
cases.rationale: README, ARCHITECTURE and PROJECT discuss the planned embedding experiment; only the audit records the review's verdict.

cases.query: What could be done later if scanning every knowledge root before each search becomes too slow?
cases.evidence_anchor: ZOMAH may later add filesystem notifications, dirty-path tracking, or another internal optimization
cases.rationale: The audit says the refresh may be optimized later without naming how; only ADR-007 names the options.

cases.query: Under what condition would a reranker be introduced into retrieval?
cases.evidence_anchor: It should be introduced only if evaluation demonstrates a retrieval failure that it has a clear job to solve.
cases.rationale: PROJECT.md mentions evaluating embeddings before a reranker; only ARCHITECTURE states the condition for adding one.

cases.query: Where on disk are model capability traces stored?
cases.evidence_anchor: `$XDG_DATA_HOME/zomah/trace.db`
cases.rationale: ADR-008 and ARCHITECTURE describe the trace contents and the persistence contract gives the zomah.db path; only README gives the trace.db location.

cases.query: Which fields may a model-originated decision proposal contain?
cases.evidence_anchor: proposals contain only an ID, statement, and rationale;
cases.rationale: ARCHITECTURE, README and the audit say model decisions are proposals and what they cannot set; only ADR-003 lists the fields a proposal contains.
